rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lowering the wing means being gentle toward the believers who follow the Prophet.
rows.anchor: { واخفض جناحك } يعنى لين لهم جناحك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who disobey are Banu Hashim and Banu Abd al-Muttalib, who did not accept faith; disavowal concerns their polytheism and unbelief.
rows.anchor: { فإن عصوك } يعنى بنى هاشم، وبنى عبد المطلب، فلم يجيبوك إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trust means rely on God: He is mighty in retribution and merciful to them by delaying punishment.
rows.anchor: حين لا يعجل عليهم بالعقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The setting is that the Prophet was invited to follow his forefathers’ religion, which Meccan unbelievers spoke about and God knows.
rows.anchor: وذلك حين دعى إلى ملة آبائه، ثم قال سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees the Prophet when he rises alone to pray.
rows.anchor: [آية: 218] وحدك إلى الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees his bowing, prostration, and standing, including when he prays with the congregation.
rows.anchor: يعنى ويرى ركوعك وسجودك وقيامك فهذا التقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears what they said when the Prophet called them to his forefathers’ religion and knows what Meccan unbelievers said.
rows.anchor: { العليم } [آية: 220] بما قال كفار مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’s family member addressed here is his wife.
rows.anchor: { إذ قال موسى لأهله } يعنى امرأته حين رأى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire Moses saw was the light of the Lord of Majesty, seen on Friday night to the mountain’s right in the Holy Land.
rows.anchor: وهو نور رب العزة جل ثناؤه، رآه ليلة الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses had lost the road and hoped to learn the route; if no one could guide him, he would bring a bright torch so they could warm themselves.
rows.anchor: أين الطريق، وقد كان تحير وترك الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What Moses reached was the fire, understood as the light of the Lord of Majesty.
rows.anchor: { فلما جآءها } يعنى النار، وهو نور رب العزة، تبارك وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those around the fire were angels; Muqatil identifies them as the blessed company in the call.
rows.anchor: { نودي أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها } يعنى الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God identifies himself as the light Moses saw.
rows.anchor: { يموسى إنه أنا الله } يقول: إن النور الذى رأيت أنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff’s trembling means it moved, and its appearance like a jinn means it looked like a snake.
rows.anchor: { وألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز } يعنى تحرك { كأنها جآن } يعنى كأنها كانت حية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses fled in fear of the snake and did not turn back; God told him not to fear, since messengers do not fear in His presence.
rows.anchor: { ولى مدبرا } من الخوف من الحية { ولم يعقب } يعنى ولم يرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of strength means many men; he cites 18:95, where strength likewise means men.
rows.anchor: { قالوا } لها: { نحن أولو قوة } يعنى عدة كثيرة فى الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their great might means bravery in battle.
rows.anchor: { وأولو بأس شديد } فى الحرب، يعنى الشجاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have stated their resources and will not go beyond what the queen decides.
rows.anchor: { والأمر إليك } يقول: قد أخبرناك بما عندنا وما نجاوز ما تقولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her people ask what she advises; Pharaoh’s question in 26:35 uses the same wording to ask for advice.
rows.anchor: يعنى ماذا تشيرين علينا، كقول فرعون لقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A king’s ruining a town means destroying it; Muqatil compares the wording to 21:22.
rows.anchor: { قالت إن الملوك إذا دخلوا قرية أفسدوها } يعنى أهلكوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invaders humiliate the town’s nobles and chiefs so they can establish their rule.
rows.anchor: { وجعلوا أعزة أهلهآ أذلة } يعنى أهانوا أشرافها وكبراءها لكى يستقيم لهم الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God confirms that kings act as the queen described.
rows.anchor: { وكذلك يفعلون } [آية: 34] كما قالت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen sends a gift to appease them over her kingdom if they are worldly people, then waits for the envoys’ answer.
rows.anchor: { وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية } أصانعهم على ملكى إن كانوا أهل دنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envoy leader was al-Mundhir ibn Amr; the gift included one hundred male and one hundred female servants dressed alike, plus two gems, one pierced and one unpierced.
rows.anchor: المنذر بن عمر، والهدية مائة وصيف، ومائة وصيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen’s test was whether Sulayman could distinguish the boys and girls and tell the box’s contents: a prophet would do so and return the gift, while a king would accept it.
rows.anchor: وقالت للوفد: إن كان نبيا، فسيميز بين الجوارى والغلمان ويخبر بما فى الحقة، ويرد الهدية فلا يقبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulayman distinguished the servants by their different hand positions while performing ablution: girls poured water over the forearm and boys over its back.
rows.anchor: ميز بين الوصفاء والوصائف من قبل الوضوء، وذلك أنه أمرهم بالوضوء فكانت الجارية تصب الماء على بطن ساعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel informed Sulayman about the gems; a worm in soft silver pulled a thread through the crooked pierced gem, and a termite drilled the other without human or jinn help.
rows.anchor: وكانت الجوهرة المثقوبة معوجة، فأتته دودة تكون فى الفضفضة وهي الرطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envoys asked for water neither from rain nor a spring; Sulayman ran horses until they sweated, strained the sweat into crystal cups, and impressed them. Gabriel told him the box’s contents; Sulayman disclosed them and returned the gift.
rows.anchor: ماء لم ينزل من السماء ولم يخرج من الأرض، فأمر بالخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulayman asks whether they would support him with wealth and says God’s gifts of Islam, prophethood, and troops are better than theirs.
rows.anchor: { أتمدونن بمال فمآ آتاني الله خير ممآ آتاكم } يقول: فما أعطانى الله تعالى من الإسلام والنبوة والجنود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People rejoice when they exchange gifts, but Sulayman does not rejoice in this gift; he wants them to accept Islam.
rows.anchor: يعنى إذا أهدى بعضكم إلى بعض، فأما أنا فلا أفرح بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulayman sends the gift back and threatens an army of jinn and humans they cannot withstand, which will expel them in disgrace.
rows.anchor: ثم قال سليمان لأمير الوفد، { ارجع إليهم } بالهدية { فلنأتينهم بجنود لا قبل لهم بها } لا طاقة لهم بها من الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will be made humiliated by the jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: { ولنخرجنهم منها أذلة وهم صاغرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s household found Moses in his chest among water and trees; Muqatil derives his name from Coptic mo (water) and si (tree).
rows.anchor: من البحر من بين الماء والشجر، وهو في التابوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses would be their enemy through their destruction and a source of grief and anger over the killing of their firstborn; linked to 26:55.
rows.anchor: { ليكون لهم عدوا } في الهلاك { وحزنا } يعني وغيظا في قتل الأبكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil repeats the verse’s judgment that Pharaoh, Haman, and their troops were wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: { إن فرعون وهامان وجنودهما كانوا خاطئين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s wife was Asiya daughter of Muzahim.
rows.anchor: { وقالت امرأت فرعون } واسمها آسية بنت مزاحم، عليها السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She argues not to kill Moses because he came from another land, not from Israel, and might benefit them or become their son.
rows.anchor: { قرت عين لي ولك لا تقتلوه } فإنا أتينا به من أرض أخرى، وليس من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not realize that Moses will cause their destruction.
rows.anchor: { وهم لا يشعرون } [آية: 9] أن هلاكهم في سببه

words: وأصبح فؤاد أم موسى فارغا إن كادت لتبدي به
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’s mother saw waves lift and lower the chest and feared he would drown; compassion nearly made her cry out and reveal to Egypt that he was her son.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنها رأت التابوت يرفعه موج ويضعه آخر، فخشيت عليه الغرق، فكادت تصيح شفقة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God steadied her heart through faith, so she believed His assurance that Moses would be returned and made a messenger.
rows.anchor: { لتكون من المؤمنين } [آية: 10] يعني من المصدقين بتوحيد الله عز وجل

words: وجاء رجل من أقصا المدينة يسعى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man was the believing Copt Hizqil ibn Sabuth; he came running on foot from the far end of the town.
rows.anchor: فجاء حزقيل بن صابوث القبطي، وهو المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egypt’s chiefs conspired to kill Moses for killing the Copt, so the man urged him to leave and assured him of his sincere advice.
rows.anchor: { يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك } بقتلك القبطي، { فاخرج } من القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses feared being killed and watched for the pursuers as he fled.
rows.anchor: يعني ينتظر الطلب، وهو هارب منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oppressors are Egypt’s polytheists; God answered by sending Gabriel to direct Moses toward Midian and giving him the staff.
rows.anchor: يعني المشركين، أهل مصر، فاستجاب الله عز وجل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses travelled from Egypt to Midian without a guide in ten days.
rows.anchor: فسار من مصر إلى مدين في عشرة أيام بغير دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without a guide, Moses feared losing the route and asked God to guide him to the straight road to Midian, which he reached.
rows.anchor: بغير دليل خشى أن يضل الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water was named for Midian, son of Abraham the Friend of God.
rows.anchor: ابن إبراهيم خليل الرحمن لصلبه، عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses found a group watering their sheep, and two women holding their flock back to water after the shepherds left.
rows.anchor: يقول: وجد موسى على الماء جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women were Shuayb’s twin daughters, Sabura and Abra; the elder was born half a day earlier. They waited until shepherds returned to pasture, then watered leftover water because their aged father could not.
rows.anchor: يعني حابستين الغنم لتسقي فضل ماء الرعاء، وهما ابنتا شعيب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’s question means “What is your situation?” They say they do not water until the shepherds leave.
rows.anchor: لهما موسى: { ما خطبكما } يعني ما أمركما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asked where the water was, lifted alone a well-covering stone that required a group, drew a bucket into the basin, and prayed for blessing.
rows.anchor: لا يزيله إلا عصابة من الناس، فرفعه موسى، عليه السلام، وحده بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assembly addressed by Pharaoh means the chiefs of his people.
rows.anchor: { وقال فرعون يأيها الملأ } يعني الأشراف من قومه

words: ما علمت لكم من إله غيري
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s claim that he knows no god for them except himself is an act of unbelief.
rows.anchor: { ما علمت لكم من إله غيري } هذا القول من فرعون كفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haman was to fire clay into bricks; Pharaoh was the first to bake bricks and build with them.
rows.anchor: يقول: أوقد النار على الطين حتى يصير اللبن أجرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ṣarḥ is a tall palace; its mortar was glass slag, and the wind made it frightening to stand on lest a person be swept away.
rows.anchor: ملاطه خبث القوارير، فكان الرجل لا يستطيع القيام عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh wanted to look for Moses’s God and claimed Moses was lying when he said God was in heaven.
rows.anchor: بما يقول: إن في السماء إلها

words: واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh and his army arrogantly rejected faith through disobedience and thought they would not return alive after death.
rows.anchor: أحياء بعد الموت في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cast Pharaoh and his troops into Egypt’s Nile; the polytheists of Egypt met their end by drowning.
rows.anchor: يعني فقذفناهم في نهر النيل الذي بمصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh and the chiefs became leaders in shirk who called people to shirk; the Egyptians followed them, and they will not be protected from punishment.
rows.anchor: { وجعلناهم أئمة } يعني قادة في الشرك { يدعون إلى النار } يعني يدعون إلى الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly curse was drowning; in the hereafter they are in the Fire.
rows.anchor: { وأتبعناهم في هذه الدنيا لعنة } يعني الغرق { ويوم القيامة } في النار { هم من المقبوحين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God addresses the Meccan unbelievers, asking where the partners they claimed He had are.
rows.anchor: [آية: 62] في الدنيا أن معي شريكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those on whom the punishment decree has fallen are the devils; the decree was declared to Iblis in 7:18.
rows.anchor: { قال الذين حق عليهم القول } يعني وجب عليهم كلمة العذاب وهم الشياطين

words: هؤلاء الذين أغوينا أغويناهم كما غوينا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils say they misled Adam’s human descendants as they themselves were astray, then disavow them; devils disown those who worshipped them.
rows.anchor: يعنون كفار بني آدم، يعني هؤلاء الذين أضللناهم كما ضللنا

words: ادعوا شركاءكم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers are told to ask their idols whether they are gods; the idols do not answer, as in 18:52.
rows.anchor: سألوهم فلم تجبهم الآلهة، نظيرها في الكهف

words: ورأوا العذاب لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They see the punishment; had they been guided from error in worldly life, they would not see punishment in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: يقول: لوأنهم كانوا مهتدين في الدنيا ما رأوا العذاب في الآخرة

words: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun was an Israelite and Moses’s cousin; Muqatil gives both their genealogies through Qohath and Levi.
rows.anchor: يعني من بني إسرائيل، وكان ابن عمه، قارون بن أصهر بن قوهث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun oppressed the Israelites because of his treasure.
rows.anchor: يقول: بغى قارون على بني إسرائيل من أجل كنزه ما له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treasures are wealth and their keys are storehouses; a company of ten to forty strong men could not carry the chests.
rows.anchor: والعصبة من عشرة أنفار إلى أربعين، فإذا كانوا أربعين

words: لا تفرح إن الله لا يحب الفرحين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here rejoice means prance, act arrogantly, and boast over wealth; God does not love the boastful and arrogant.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا تمرح ولا تبطر ولا تفخر بما أوتيت من الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun should use the wealth and good God gave him to seek the hereafter, meaning the Garden.
rows.anchor: { الدار الآخرة } يعني دار الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not forget your portion means do not abandon your share of worldly life: working in it for the hereafter.
rows.anchor: { ولا تنس نصيبك } يعني ولا تترك حظك { من الدنيا } أن تعمل فيها لآخرتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing good means giving charity and doing good works in ways that please God.
rows.anchor: { وأحسن } العطية في الصدقة والخير فيما يرضى الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not commit disobedience in response to God’s beneficence; God does not love corrupters.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا تعمل فيها بالمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun says his wealth was given to him on account of knowledge or good God knew to be in him.
rows.anchor: يقول: على خير علمه الله عز وجل عندي

words: أولم يعلم أن الله قد أهلك من قبله من القرون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed earlier generations for rejecting their messengers, including people stronger and wealthier than Qarun, such as Nimrod.
rows.anchor: من قارون { قوة } وبطشا { وأكثر جمعا } من الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Criminals of this community are not asked about earlier nations’ sins, since God has recorded and knows their evil deeds.
rows.anchor: يقول: ولا يسأل مجرمو هذه الأمة عن ذنوب الأمم الخالية الذين عذبوا في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with knowledge address people who wished for wealth like Qarun’s, reminding them of the promised afterlife reward.
rows.anchor: { وقال الذين أوتوا العلم } بما وعد الله في الآخرة للذين تمنوا مثل مما أعطي قارون

words: ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s reward is better than Qarun’s worldly gifts for those who affirm God’s oneness and do good works.
rows.anchor: خير مما أوتي قارون في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It refers to righteous deeds, which are granted only to the patient.
rows.anchor: يعني الأعمال الصالحة، يعني ولا يؤتاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commanded the earth to obey Moses; it seized Qarun up to his feet. Qarun appealed to kinship, but Moses ordered the earth to swallow him, and he sinks a man’s height daily until Judgment.
rows.anchor: { فخسفنا به } يعني بقارون، وذلك أن الله عز وجل أمر الأرض أن تطيع موسى، عليه السلام، فأمر موسى الأرض أن تأخذ قارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites accused Moses of destroying Qarun to seize his wealth and house; three days later God swallowed Qarun’s house and possessions, ending their accusation.
rows.anchor: فقالت بنو إسرائيل: إن موسى إنما أهلك قارون حتى يأخذ ماله وداره، فخسف الله عز وجل بعد قارون بثلاثة أيام

words: فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun had no troop to protect him from God and could not prevent the punishment of being swallowed.
rows.anchor: يقول الله عز وجل: لم يكن لقارون جند يمنعونه من الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s command to worship God means affirm His oneness; fear Him means fear God, which is better than worshipping idols.
rows.anchor: يعنى وحدوا الله، { واتقوه } ، يعنى واخشوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification means that this is better if they know, although in fact they do not know.
rows.anchor: [آية: 16]، ولكنكم لا تعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fabricate a lie by making and sculpting idols by hand, then claiming these objects are gods; 37:96 says God created them and what they make.
rows.anchor: ثم تزعمون أنها آلهة كذبا وأنتم تنحتونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot provide sustenance, so people should seek provision from God and worship Him by affirming His oneness.
rows.anchor: ن يقول: لا يقدرون { لكم رزقا } ، على رزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should thank God for His blessings because they return to Him alive after death.
rows.anchor: واشكروا الله فى النعم، فإن مصيركم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grant was to Abraham; Jacob was Isaac’s son in the Holy Land.
rows.anchor: يعنى لإبراهيم، { إسحاق ويعقوب } ابن إسحاق بالأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s descendants with prophethood are Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob; the book means Abraham’s scrolls.
rows.anchor: { والكتاب } ، يعنى صحف إبراهيم، { وآتيناه أجره }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s worldly reward was good remembrance and praise among all religions for obeying God, enduring the fire, breaking idols, and proceeding to sacrifice his son; all claim him. His afterlife status is among the righteous, as in 16:122.
rows.anchor: لمضيه على رضوان الله حين ألقى فى النار، وكسر الأصنام، ومضيه على ذبح ابنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot’s people committed the sin of anal intercourse with men at night; none before them in the worlds had done it, and they did it only with strangers.
rows.anchor: يعنى المعصية، يعنى إتيان الرجال فى أدبارهم ليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting the road means assaulting travelers: Lot’s people threw stones and clods at passersby from their meeting place.
rows.anchor: يعنى المسافر، وذلك أنهم إذا جلسوا فى ناديهم، يعنى فى مجالسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoing in their assembly means throwing stones at people.
rows.anchor: يعنى فى مجالسكم المنكر، يعنى الحذف بالحجارة

words: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Lot forbade indecency and wrongdoing, his people demanded the punishment he said was coming in this world.
rows.anchor: حين نهاهم عن الفاحشة والمنكر، { إلا أن قالوا } للوط، عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot calls his people corrupters because of their sexual sin and asks God to vindicate his warning of punishment, which they denied.
rows.anchor: فدعا لوط ربه عز وجل ف { قال رب انصرني على القوم المفسدين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed Lot’s people by the earth’s swallowing them and a shower of stones; Lot had warned them of the punishment.
rows.anchor: فأهلكهم الله عز وجل بالخسف والحصب، وكان لوط، عليه السلام، قد أنذرهم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not create the heavens and earth in vain; He created them for a matter that will come.
rows.anchor: { خلق الله السماوات والأرض بالحق } لم يخلقهما باطلا لغير شىء خلقهما لأمر هو كائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation of the heavens and earth is a lesson for those who affirm God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: يقول: إن فى خلقهما لعبرة للمصدقين بتوحيد الله عز وجل

words: اتل ما أوحي إليك من الكتاب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to recite the revealed Qur’an to the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: { اتل ما أوحي إليك من الكتاب } يعنى اقرأ على أهل الكتاب ما أنزل إليك من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer means performing it fully.
rows.anchor: { وأقم } يعنى وأتم { الصلاة إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشآء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indecency means sins and wrongdoing means what is unrecognized; a person praying to God refrains from them while praying, until finishing.
rows.anchor: يعنى عن المعاصى { والمنكر } يعنى المنكر ما لا يعرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When one remembers God in prayer, God remembers that person for good; God’s remembrance is greater than the worshipper’s remembrance of Him.
rows.anchor: { ولذكر الله أكبر } يعنى إذا صليت لله تعالى فذكرته فذكرك الله بخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what people do in their prayers.
rows.anchor: { والله يعلم ما تصنعون } [آية: 45] فى صلاتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created people and will recreate them alive after death; they return to Him for recompense according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: يقول: الله بدأ الناس فخلقهم، ثم يعيدهم فى الآخرة

words: ولم يكن لهم من شركائهم شفعاء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day the Meccan unbelievers despair of intercession from their angelic partners, who disavow those who worshipped them.
rows.anchor: يعنى كفار مكة من شفاعة الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reckoning, people separate into the Garden and Fire and never meet again.
rows.anchor: بعد الحساب إلى الجنة، وإلى النار، فلا يجتمعون أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who did good works are in the Garden’s gardens, honored and enjoying its blessings.
rows.anchor: يعنى فى بساتين يكرمون وينعمون فيها وهي الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous believers have gardens of bliss and do not die; God’s true promise is fulfilled, and He is mighty in His kingdom and wise in assigning them the Garden.
rows.anchor: فإنه منجز لهم ما وعدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil notes fronting in the phrase: the seven heavens stand without supports, and people see them standing so.
rows.anchor: يقول: هن قائمات ليس لهن عمد

words: وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God placed mountains in the earth to keep it from shifting beneath people.
rows.anchor: يقول: لئلا تزول بكم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created every kind of creature in the earth.
rows.anchor: يقول: خلق في الأرض من كل دابة

words: وأنزلنا من السماء ماء فأنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent rain from heaven and brought forth every beautiful kind of plant in the earth.
rows.anchor: يقول: فأجرينا بالماء في الأرض

words: هذا خلق الله فأروني ماذا خلق الذين من دونه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation described is God’s work; the challenge is directed at Meccan unbelievers and their worship of angels, as in Saba and Ahqaf.
rows.anchor: { هذا } الذي ذكر { خلق الله } عز وجل وصنعه { فأروني } يعني كفار مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are in manifest loss.
rows.anchor: [آية: 11] يعني في خسران مبين

words: من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked who created the heavens and earth, the unbelievers answer God; most nonetheless do not know His oneness.
rows.anchor: بتوحيد الله عز وجل، ثم عظم نفسه عز وجل، فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creatures in the heavens and earth are God’s servants and belong to His dominion.
rows.anchor: { لله ما في السماوات والأرض }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is independent of His creatures and praised among them in His sovereignty.
rows.anchor: [آية: 26] عند خلقه في سلطانه

words: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر ما نفدت كلمات الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If every tree became pens and seven seas supplied ink for all creation to record God’s knowledge and wonders, the pens and seas would run out while His knowledge, words, and wonders would not.
rows.anchor: يعنى علم الله يقول: لو أن كل شجرة ذات ساق على وجه الأرض بريت أقلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty in His kingdom and wise in His command; no one can comprehend His knowledge.
rows.anchor: فى أمره، يخبر الناس أن أحدا لا يدرك علمه

words: ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Qurashis Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Abu al-Ashdayn (Asid ibn Kilda), and Munabbih and Nabih, sons of al-Hajjaj ibn al-Sabaq ibn Hudhayfah al-Sahmi.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبي بن خلف، وأبى الأشدين واسمه أسيد بن كلدة، ومنبه ونبيه ابنى الحجاج بن السباق بن حذيفة السهمي

words: ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They objected that God created people in stages but, the Prophet claimed, would resurrect everyone together in one hour.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن الله خلقنا أطوارا، نطفة، علقة، مضغة، عظاما، لحما

words: ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers that creating and raising all people is as easy as doing so for one person.
rows.anchor: أيها الناس جميعا على الله سبحانه في القدرة، إلا كخلق نفس واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears what they said about creation and resurrection and sees all things.
rows.anchor: لما قالوا من الخلق والبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are Meccan unbelievers, who bow before God and plead to return to worldly life to do good because they are certain of resurrection.
rows.anchor: { ولو ترى } يا محمد { إذ المجرمون } يعني عز وجل كفار مكة { ناكسوا رءوسهم عند ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have given every sinful soul its guidance or explanation, but His decree of punishment stands and He will fill Hell with unbelieving humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: { ولو شئنا لآتينا } يعني لأعطينا { كل نفس } فاجرة { هداها } يعني بيانها { ولكن حق القول مني } يعني وجب العذاب مني

words: لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment decree echoes God’s statement to Iblis after he disobeyed the command to prostrate to Adam, quoted at 38:85.
rows.anchor: والقول الذي وجب من الله عز وجل لقوله لإبليس يوم عصاه في السجود لآدم، عليه السلام

words: فذوقوا بما نسيتم لقاء يومكم هذا إنا نسيناكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guards say “We forgot you,” meaning they leave unbelievers in punishment for abandoning belief in resurrection.
rows.anchor: تقول الخزنة: إنا تركناكم في العذاب

words: وذوقوا عذاب الخلد بما كنتم تعملون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment does not end, and they must taste it for their unbelief and denial.
rows.anchor: الذي لا ينقطع { بما كنتم تعملون } [آية: 14] من الكفر والتكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden of Abode is the believers’ refuge.
rows.anchor: { أما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فلهم } في الآخرة { جنات المأوى } مأوى المؤمنين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unattributed alternative says the Garden of Abode is the resting place of martyrs’ spirits.
rows.anchor: ويقال: مأوى أرواح الشهداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden is their welcome and reward for their deeds.
rows.anchor: مأوى أرواح الشهداء { نزلا بما كانوا يعملون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who disobey, meaning unbelievers, have the Fire as destination; when it surges it throws them upward, but angels strike them with maces and they fall to its depths.
rows.anchor: كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها أعيدوا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Hell surges, it throws people to the top; angels meet those trying to escape with maces and strike them back to the bottom.
rows.anchor: إذا جاشت ألقت الناس في أعلى النار، فيريدون الخروج

words: ذوقوا عذاب النار الذي كنتم به تكذبون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guards tell them to taste the Fire they denied, rejecting both resurrection and the coming punishment.
rows.anchor: بالبعث وبالعذاب بأنه ليس كائنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lesser punishment was the seven-year Meccan famine, when unbelievers ate bones, dead bodies, carrion, and dogs because they rejected the Prophet.
rows.anchor: { ولنذيقنهم } يعني كفار مكة { من العذاب الأدنى } يعني الجوع الذي أصابهم في السنين السبع بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greater punishment was killing at Badr, more severe than the famine; it was meant to bring them from unbelief back to faith.
rows.anchor: [آية: 21] من الكفر إلى الإيمان
